definitions.explanation: The slow-moving mammal of Central and South American rainforests that hangs upside down from branches. Written in katakana as an animal name; it is named after {怠|なま}け{者|もの}, a lazy person.

examples.japanese: ナマケモノ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ゆっくり→ゆっくり：00910_yukkuri⟧⟦{動|うご}く→動く：00904_ugoku⟧。
⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{枝|えだ}→枝：02181_eda⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ナマケモノ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ぶら{下|さ}がっている→ぶら下がる：05541_burasagaru⟧。
examples.english: A sloth is hanging from a tree branch.

examples.japanese: ナマケモノ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一日|いちにち}→一日：00942_ichinichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{大半|たいはん}→大半：00400_taihan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{過|す}ごし→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧、⟦{地面|じめん}→地面：00125_jimen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{下|お}りる⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{週|しゅう}→週：03204_shuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{一度|いちど}→一度：01312_ichido⟧ほどだ。
examples.english: Sloths spend most of the day in the trees and come down to the ground only about once a week.

notes:
Spelling tells the two words apart: katakana ナマケモノ is the animal, and kanji ⟦{怠|なま}け{者|もの}→怠け者：16970_namakemono⟧ is a lazy person. Calling a person ナマケモノ in katakana is a playful way of saying they are lazy.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{怠|なま}け{者|もの}→怠け者：16970_namakemono⟧: lazybones, a lazy person

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{怠|なま}ける→怠ける：02379_namakeru⟧: to be lazy, to slack off
